data.narrative:
Mainspring Energy is a Seed-stage company in the Climate & Energy sector that has raised over $650M to date. The comparable universe consists of one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support a robust Peer-Median valuation method.

Stage-Progression analysis, grounded in total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. Using $9M as the reference point derived from the capital-raised proxy, this method yields an implied valuation of $22M. This represents the sole applicable triangulation method given the sparse peer comparability at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $19M to $26M, with a median point of $22M. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of single-method triangulation and the absence of narrow-set peer validation. Key risk factors include the limited applicability of Stage-Progression alone, sensitivity to the $9M baseline assumption, and lack of same-stage transaction data in frontier climate technology. Investors should treat this range as indicative rather than definitive and supplement with operational due diligence on capital efficiency and path to revenue.
